name: Propaganda poster
block: Style: a mid-20th-century public poster in the treatment named below.

print.line: Treatment: a screen print in flat inks
print.describe: a mid-century screen-printed public poster: flat inks of brick red, cream and near black (plus mustard or navy), hard edges, halftone and misregistration, silhouettes of industry or the city, heroic idealised figures, block-letter words where asked, sunburst rays only when asked

painted.line: Treatment: a 1950s realist illustration poster in opaque oil paint
painted.describe: a 1950s realist painted public poster: opaque oil paint like a mid-century magazine illustration, true-to-life proportions, calm idealised faces with restrained emotion, smooth academic modelling, no outlines, one plain flat background colour or a painted sky, one big painted word or none

jet.describe: a 1960s jet-age graphic public poster: flat angular shapes, sharp diagonals and speed streaks, machines cutting across the frame, people as bold heroic profiles in a corner, a flat palette of yellow, red, grey, black and white

montage.describe: a 1930s constructivist photomontage poster: high-contrast black-and-white photographs joined edge to edge with clean razor-sharp cuts, colour only from flat red bars, bands and blocks (and at most one object in one flat colour), huge machines against a photographed sky, crowds of faces looking up, banners allowed
